name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals CoagCascade DX-11 Disseminated Clotting Reversal Agent
product_name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals CoagCascade DX-11 Disseminated Clotting Reversal Agent
description:
The CoagCascade DX-11 is a precision pharmacological agent delivered via pressurized auto-injector that rapidly reverses pathological clotting cascades — including those triggered by synthetic blood products like HemaForge RX-7 — without inducing systemic hemorrhage. The formulation uses tiered enzymatic inhibitors that deactivate fibrin cross-linking in a staged sequence, preventing the catastrophic rebound bleeding that plagued earlier anticoagulant interventions. Each injector contains a proprietary sensor-reactive compound that reads local thrombin concentration and modulates dosing in real time, making it effective across a wide range of clotting severity without requiring a calibrated medical professional.

The DX-11 was originally developed under contract for Meridian General Hospital's trauma wards, where augmentation-related coagulopathies had become a leading cause of post-operative death. The rise of black-market implant surgeries performed outside sterile environments created a second, larger market — street surgeons now stock the DX-11 as a standard kit item. Its auto-titrating mechanism means even an untrained operator can administer it safely in most cases, though overdose in patients with pre-existing vascular grafts remains a documented complication.

The injector housing is a matte gunmetal cylinder roughly the size of a thick marker, with a biometric safety ring that can be disabled by licensed clinicians or bypassed by anyone with moderate technical skill. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals sells the clinical-grade version exclusively through Tier 2+ licensed pharmacies, but a nearly identical grey-market formulation circulates in the Undersprawl under the name 'ClotBreak,' differing primarily in its lack of the concentration-sensing module — making dosing a calculated risk.

social_impact: The DX-11's widespread availability has fundamentally shifted the risk calculus of unsanctioned augmentation surgery in Meridian 88's lower tiers — what was once a near-certain death sentence from clotting complications is now a survivable, if still dangerous, procedure. This has accelerated the rate of unlicensed body modification in Tiers 4 and 5, simultaneously alarming corporate medical monopolies (who lose revenue to grey-market operators) and spurring Lazarus Pharmaceuticals to lobby for tighter distribution controls while quietly continuing to supply the grey-market chains through deniable intermediaries.
story_hooks: A Tier 5 street surgeon is found dead with a full case of DX-11 stolen — someone is stockpiling reversal agents, suggesting a planned mass-augmentation event or sabotage of a synthetic blood supply
A player character suffers a coagulopathy cascade mid-mission and has only a grey-market ClotBreak without the concentration sensor — they must estimate dosing under fire
Lazarus Pharmaceuticals hires fixers to track down whoever reverse-engineered the DX-11 formula and is selling it to an unlicensed manufacturer in the Port District
A corporate assassin is using DX-11 overdoses staged as medical accidents to eliminate augmented targets whose vascular grafts make them uniquely vulnerable
